To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

PLCE1 and MICA/B SNPs associated with dengue shock are likely to be involved in differential protein binding patterns and protein structure modification, and these alterations may be involved in the pathogenesis and progression of the disease.

the SNPs associated with dengue shock (DSS) syndrome in the PLCE1 and MICA genes have an effect on the structure and transcription of these proteins, which may be associated with the pathophysiology of DSS.
PLCE1 and the MICB genes are associated with DSS and the SNP rs2274223 in PLCE1 induces structural change in PLCε protein and represses its expression in DSS.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the functional analysis of SNPs associated with the risk of developing severe dengue.
the impact of PLCE1 and MHC class I-related chain B (MICB) gene SNPs associated with dengue shock syndromes (DSS) on the transcriptional and translational regulation of the genes.
the identification and analysis of SNPs in the PLCE1 and MICA genes associated with the development of DSS.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the rs2274223 SNP in the PLCE1 gene induces a structural change in the protein, which in turn alters the protein's function.
the SNPs rs2274223 and rs1051798 are associated with DSS and may contribute to the development of DSS by altering transcriptional and functional regulation of PLCE1 and/or MICB genes.

the SNPs associated with dengue shock are not only responsible for the development of DSS but also for the differential binding of transcription factors and proteins with the PLCE1 and the MICB genes.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the PLCE1 and MICA SNPs associated with dengue shock may be responsible for the differential expression of PLCE1 and the MICA in the pathogenesis.
the deleterious SNP rs2274223 in PLCE1 gene induces structural changes in the C2 domains, with the mutant amino acid residue more positively charged and the chromatin-repressed expression in DSS.
SNPs in PLCA1 and MICB associated with DSS alter the protein coding, transcription and translation, and protein structure, which could be the possible mechanisms for the pathogenesis of dengue.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the SNPs in PLDE1 and MICB are associated with differential protein binding patterns and structural changes in the proteins, which can alter the expression of the genes and their protein function.
the SNP in PLCE1 gene is associated with a structural change in the protein and a transcriptional repression, which could be a potential cause of DSS in dengue patients.
the SNPs in PLDE1 and MICB are associated with the development of dSS.
